rows.notes: Bounded to the six most-contested nations so the rupture count is a property of the design rather than of the map size.

rows.requirement: The record can be destroyed and the hole stays visible: a won war erases the lines naming the provinces it took, replaces them with a dated lacuna carrying a count of what was lost, plants the victor's pantheon on those provinces, and keeps the founders recorded in founding_culture.
rows.result_metric: Met - 4 of 6 worlds in the seed spread lost part of their record to a war. A conquered province is asserted to keep a founding_culture distinct from its (conquered) culture, so the erasure is of the record, never of the fact.
rows.notes: Ben, 2026-08-02: 'don't be afraid to have parts of the record erased when two nations go to war'.

rows.requirement: Corporate focus derives from the corp's HOME PROVINCE (ancient endowment plus the movement up the value chain for early industrialisers), the authored focus-weighting table is retired on that path, and diversity is a world-level reject-and-reroll against a floor on the SET rather than a quota on any member.
rows.result_metric: Met - the three tier rules assert directly on focus_from_province, and the world-level floor holds across the generated corporation set (5 extraction / 1 processing / 2 trade on seed 0). corp_terrain_matrix passes, so every generated corp is still terrain-viable. Player-corp parity is unchanged - same province read, same reroll, no special case.
rows.notes: Per-province rather than per-nation deliberately: a nation average would make every corp in a nation alike and destroy the specialists premise.

rows.requirement: No regression across the logic tier, and any divergence in the AI skill goldens is explained rather than suppressed.
rows.result_metric: Met - 39/39 CTest green. Two harnesses needed work: history_ladder_harness's H4 stage-ordering assertion was NARROWED (it demanded every line in the recorded-history window be strictly older than the next, which only held while the ladder owned that window alone), and ai_skill_harness's MSVC golden set was RE-BLESSED. Every AI divergence was upward - net worth rose on seeds 0/2/4 while solvency and survival stayed in band - which is the intended consequence of corps anchoring to provinces that actually industrialised.
rows.notes: A pre-existing unrelated break was also fixed: trade_routes_harness's hand-declared CMake link set never picked up river_generation.cpp after BL-170 landed, so it failed to link. Removed the hand-declaration per the file's own guidance on that rot.

rows.requirement: With spectating on, the strategic tier evaluates the player corp on the same staggered cadence as every other corp - it builds, dials, surveys and trades like a rival.
rows.notes: Asserted as a controlled A/B rather than literally, and the reason is a finding in its own right (NR-231): the generated player corp on seed 0 is insolvent with zero extractors, so a four-family bar there would have asserted that corp is rich rather than that the guard lifted. The harness instead seats the best-endowed corp - picked by a stable property, not by outcome - which reaches 4/4 verb families spectated and 0 decisions seated+played. Same corp, same world, same seed, only the seat varies.

rows.requirement: With spectating OFF the run is unchanged byte-for-byte: same seed, same tick count, identical world::state_hash against the pre-BL-409 build.
rows.notes: VERIFIED, not assumed. The guard changes were stashed and the harness run against the genuine pre-BL-409 corp_ai.cpp: pre-change unspectated state_hash 3CBAD1D44EE71EDE, post-change unspectated 3CBAD1D44EE71EDE - identical, and baked in as the harness golden. The same pre-change build also put the SPECTATED hash at 3CBAD1D44EE71EDE (the flag was inert), so R3's 'spectating moves the world' row correctly FAILED against it - both halves have teeth rather than passing vacuously.

rows.requirement: A spectated run is itself deterministic: same seed, spectating on, N ticks, run twice - identical state_hash both times.
rows.notes: Three rows: same seed + spectating + N ticks run twice gives an identical state_hash; the player corp's own decision stream is reproducible under spectate; and a spectated run diverges from a played one. Also asserted that admitting the player shifts NO rival's cadence slot, since the index is over the sorted corp set.

rows.requirement: Player-press affordances are disabled (not hidden) under spectate, so the mode reads as a window rather than as a broken game.
rows.notes: NOT DONE. UI work in files the BL-409 agent did not own, and deliberately left rather than reached for. Player-press affordances (construction placement, order entry, workforce dials) still respond under spectate. Needs doing before spectator mode is usable, but it does not block the guard. rows.requirement: A battle is one deterministic evaluation of unit-type matchup x formation doctrine x BL-233's terrain scalars (terrain_defence/terrain_attrition/terrain_resistance) x supply state x season, over integer arithmetic with explicit index tie-breaks (no floats in the outcome path).
rows.result_metric: Met - resolve_battle takes both army stacks, doctrine rows, terrain, season and supply and returns a deterministic battle_outcome; tie broken toward defender. All-integer/per-mille arithmetic; harness asserts identical inputs -> identical outputs and a terrain-flips-the-outcome scenario.
rows.notes: This is BL-233's terrain scalars' intended consumer per HISTORY.md's BL-224 note - first real use, not a new terrain model.

rows.requirement: Doctrine is expressed purely as modifier data against the matchup matrix and terrain scalars (a doctrine row, not procedural maneuver logic) - adding a doctrine never requires touching the resolve function.
rows.result_metric: Met - doctrine_row{frontal_bonus, flank_fragility, mountain_penalty, siege_stance} is pure data; harness instantiates two distinct doctrine_row values driving the same resolve_battle to opposite outcomes on different terrain.

rows.requirement: The same resolve function is reachable from both the Era -1 sim path and the existing 1960+ era combat path (engine-parity contract) - no sandbox-only combat rule.

rows.requirement: The withdrawal-pricing property is re-derived honestly at the new swing rather than relaxed to pass: any late exit that costs LESS than an early one must be explained by the withdrawing side's deficit narrowing.
rows.notes: C3 restructured from a blanket "every seed strictly increasing" (a property of the NARROW swing, not of the design) into two checks: a majority remain monotone, AND explained == inversions is a strict equality, so an unexplained inversion fails the harness. Net sharper, not looser. Measured: 8/9 seeds monotone, 2/2 inversions explained by a narrowed deficit. Reviewed in the integrating session and confirmed mathematically sound (withdrawal is checked before each round, so the trace index is the withdrawal-instant state).
